population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: ever 32.0% − current 23.5% = 8.5% of adults used and are off now. New ever-users since 2030 = 32.0 − 26.5 = 5.5 pts, split 4.3 on and 1.2 already off. The 2030 cohort (26.5 pts): of the 18.8 then on, 11.0 stayed on and 7.8 stopped. Those 7.8 joined the 7.7 already off for a pool of 15.5. Of that pool, 8.2 restarted (53% over two years, consistent with the parent's 55%), so 11.0 + 8.2 = 19.2 on and 7.3 off. Totals: on 19.2 + 4.3 = 23.5; off 7.3 + 1.2 = 8.5. Cycled: 8.9 pts had cycled by 2030, plus ~3.0 pts of first-time restarts among the 8.2 restarters, gives 11.9 of 32.0 = 37%. The rise is driven by structural stops: the liraglutide recall, the 2×90-day cessation caps, and the Medicare transition month in Jan 2032. Users: ~63.2M of ~269M adults. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23 give 2.54 + 8.75 + 9.00 + 3.22 = 23.5. Income thirds average (28 + 23.5 + 19)/3 = 23.5. 18–29 rose from 10 to 12.7, partly through military, police and shift-worker programmes and partly through vaping cessation. 65+ rose only from 12 to 14 (~8.7M) despite permanent Medicare coverage, because the fracture communication made clinicians slower to start women over 70 and made some users stop. Off-drug: ~22.9M adults who used and stopped, plus ~183M who never used. The never-users are now mostly people who opted out on purpose, older women steered away, and the uninsured near-poor in non-expansion states. Pediatric: 1.0% of ~73M ≈ 730k under-18s. About 115k are aged 6–11, and growth was capped by the 2031 generic liraglutide shortage. The first interim registry bone-accrual data (Jun 2032) are inconclusive.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the Medicare Obesity and Metabolic Health Act (year-end health package, Dec 2031) replaced the GLP-1 Bridge with permanent Part D coverage from Jan 2032. The $50 copay is retained. Blended federal payment is $285/month (semaglutide at its negotiated price of ~$274, tirzepatide higher). The Act requires a DEXA at initiation and every two years for 65+, plus documented resistance-training counselling. Medicare pays 15% of fills ≈ 9.5M users (8.7M aged 65+, 0.8M disabled under-65): 9.5M × $285 × 12 ≈ $32.5B/yr, of which the obesity-indication subset is ~4.0M × $285 × 12 ≈ $13.7B. Medicaid: the same Act gives 90% FMAP for incretins in states that adopt a body-composition visit standard, and 34 states plus DC have opted in. Medicaid pays 15% ≈ 9.5M users at $285: ≈ $32.5B/yr combined, roughly $28B federal. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program: renewed at $5.8B for FY2032, still discretionary. 2.1M liraglutide users × $120 post-recall contract × 12 ≈ $3.0B, plus 1.1M semaglutide (cessation/AUD) × $199 × 12 ≈ $2.6B, ≈ $5.6B. Military/VA: 3% ≈ 1.9M users (≈0.25M active and reserve, 0.75M TRICARE dependents and under-65 retirees, 0.9M VA) × ~$240 federal-ceiling price × 12 ≈ $5.5B. Public payers together cover 38% of users, more than commercial at 34%.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 80+ semaglutide brands at $10–50/month and the first approved tirzepatide generics (2031). Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China sell generic semaglutide, and generic oral semaglutide is sold in ~180 countries. US Paragraph IV settlements set generic semaglutide entry for 2033, so there is still no US generic at end-2032.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~63.2M users: commercial 34% (21.5M), Medicare 15% (9.5M), Medicaid 15% (9.5M), HRSA 5% (3.2M), military/VA 3% (1.9M), cash/direct 14% (8.8M), gray 14% (8.8M) = 100% and 63.2M. Price shock (Apr 2031): an FDA import alert on three Indian semaglutide API makers, a sterility recall by the largest HRSA generic liraglutide supplier, and the scheduled second step of the Section 232 tariff. TrumpRx cash rose from $349 to $399 (semaglutide) and from $449 to $499 (tirzepatide); the oral start dose rose from $199 to $229. HRSA's liraglutide contract went from $85 to $120. Wegovy list is still $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499 (allocated). MariTide lists at $1,599. The tirzepatide + bimagrumab regimen lists at $2,149 (allocated; no Medicare formulary decision yet). Gray share fell from 18% to 14% as the import alert raised Indian pen prices to $15–60 plus shipping and pushed 503A 'personalised' compounded semaglutide to $179–299. Research-use retatrutide vials are $150–300. 'Focus/calm' wellness subscriptions (~2.7M) sit inside cash and gray. Employer weight-management coverage slipped from 57% to 55% as plans pushed retirees to Medicare. Cessation and AUD coverage is mandated regardless.

GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)

alcohol use disorder (injectable semaglutide, Jun 2030; oral semaglutide, Feb 2031)

research-peptide retatrutide and, since 2032, gray-market 'bima' vials in gyms
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. MariTide (BLA filed Jul 2030) was approved Sep 2031 as the first monthly agent, efficacy ~18–20%. Lilly's tirzepatide + bimagrumab phase 3 (begun 2029) read out Feb 2031: ~24% weight loss with roughly half the lean-mass fraction of loss seen on tirzepatide alone. The BLA was filed May 2031 and approved Sep 2032, 16 months later, inside the 12-month floor. That realises the muscle-preserving driver, but the label has lean-mass and strength endpoints only, no fracture outcomes, and a fracture-outcome trial is required post-approval. The marketing line 'the skinny-frail problem, solved' is the company's; the label does not say it. Survodutide is still under review, with an advisory committee set for early 2033. Amycretin's resubmission is pending Novo's second facility reinspection. The new indications are supplements: vaping cessation and oral AUD. Retatrutide postmarketing anhedonia data arrived Jun 2031. US generic semaglutide is settled for 2033 entry. The incretin market is ≈$160B in 2032, driven by US public-payer volume and tariff-lifted net prices.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation; higher in gray-market users and in recruits started during basic training.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established; persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has passed ~58,000 filed and tolled claims, and three of five bellwethers have gone to plaintiffs.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA still declines a persistent-gastroparesis label. Settlement talks were reported in 2032 and nothing is final. Reserves were raised.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rising in absolute numbers with the larger user base and retatrutide use.
No causal confirmation in 10-year data and low absolute risk. Claims inside the MDL keep growing anyway.

Now a recognised population problem. Medicare claims show sarcopenia diagnoses ~1.5–1.7× in 65+ users after more than 2 years, with excess falls concentrated in unmonitored, low-protein and liraglutide users. Bimagrumab combinations reduce the lean fraction lost in trials, but only the affluent can get them.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Sep 2031) moved lean-mass loss into the class Warnings section. The Medicare Act makes DEXA and strength counselling statutory for 65+. The 90% Medicaid FMAP requires a body-composition visit. HRSA sites are still exempt.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare claims analysis (JAMA, Sep 2031): hip fracture HR 1.36 in 65+ users on drug more than 2 years, higher in women over 70 and in cyclers. That is modelled at ~15,000 excess hip fractures a year among ~8.7M older users, against a baseline of ~0.5%/yr. Interim pediatric registry data are inconclusive.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings upgrade; DEXA statutory under Medicare. Guidelines now recommend antiresorptive co-therapy consideration for women 65+. No boxed warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Stress fractures in military trainees and young shift workers
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A cluster of tibial and metatarsal stress fractures among basic trainees started on semaglutide at Fort Jackson and Lackland, with an unclear denominator.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: TRADOC review (2032). DoD instruction now bars initiation during the first 8 weeks of basic training; existing users continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Retatrutide postmarketing data (Jun 2031): clinically meaningful anhedonia-scale increase in ~9% at top dose vs ~4% comparator, dose-dependent and largely reversible on dose reduction. Surveys hold at ~10–15% of long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Added to the Adverse Reactions section of the retatrutide label only, not Warnings. FTC consent orders with four wellness brands (2032) bar claims of 'FDA-recognised calm'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Structural stops multiplied: the 2031 liraglutide recall, cessation course caps, Medicaid waiver lockouts and military separation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation ongoing; the Medicare Act includes no continuity guarantee for HRSA users who age in.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein insufficiency strengthen, and now feed into the sarcopenia and fracture analyses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; the Medicare counselling visit includes a protein screen.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult and nine of adolescent follow-up. ~115k children aged 6–11 are on drug. Interim bone-accrual Z-scores show a small, non-significant deficit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry ongoing; FDA asked for an extended 6–11 study.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre calls are flat after the import alert, but the mix is shifting toward unknown-purity research peptides and gray-market bimagrumab 'bima' vials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert on three Indian API makers; warning letters; first federal indictment of a research-peptide distributor (2032); still no prosecution of individual users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; higher in research-peptide users.
Common but mostly mild in trials; real-world use is only weeks old.

food_and_beverage.state: With nearly one adult in four on drug, volume in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks keeps falling at the 2028–30 pace. Majors have finished divesting indulgent brands to private equity. 'Bone and muscle' formats (protein, calcium, vitamin D, creatine) are the fastest-growing grocery segment after the fracture communication. Medicare Advantage plans pay for protein-shake benefits in some markets.

alcohol.state: Oral AUD approval and parity coverage reach the heavy-drinking core. US spirits volume falls for a fifth year and beer contracts. States report shortfalls in tobacco excise and Master Settlement Agreement payments as vaping cessation bites, and two states' tobacco-settlement bonds were downgraded. Non-alcoholic and premium single-serve lines grow.

restaurants.state: Value-volume chains keep closing units in mid-income suburbs. Fine dining and protein-forward fast casual are steady. Alcohol attach rates are down again, and bar closures concentrate in college and military towns.

apparel.state: Size runs keep widening both ways. 'Athletic-cut' grows, and military uniform contractors re-grade size tables.

fitness.state: Statutory strength counselling and the fracture warnings send older adults to resistance training. YMCA and SilverSneakers-style programmes report record 65+ enrolment, and DEXA studios multiply. A gym-floor gray market now sells 'bima' alongside retatrutide.

insurance.state: Commercial pharmacy trend eases to ~+9% as Medicare takes retirees and dual-eligible users. Cessation and AUD mandates still force coverage. Adherence gating spreads. Plans are fighting over whether the bimagrumab add-on is 'medically necessary'.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on volume and owns the muscle-preserving category. Amgen enters with MariTide. Novo is stabilising on the Medicare negotiated price. Generic liraglutide makers lost share after the recall. MDL reserves were raised again.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on is unremarkable; being off invites a question, at the doctor, at work and on a date. The body still says who paid. Lean and muscled means a coach and maybe 'bima'. Thin and soft-shouldered means a public pen. A cane at 72 now prompts a quiet guess about the drug.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thin no longer divides the classes, because a public payer covers 38% of users. Muscle and bone density do. In San Antonio, a military and Medicare town, the drug is everywhere: recruits at Lackland, VA patients at Audie Murphy, retirees on Part D. The differences show in who has DEXA appointments and who has a strength coach.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller meals are the default. Church potlucks and quinceañeras plan for half the food they used to. 'Protein first' is a family rule, pushed hard on grandparents after the fracture headlines.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule out of habit. 'Off' needs a reason: 'trying for a baby', 'military separation', 'didn't like the grey'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of every kind is treated as a clinical variable, and an unmedicated craving reads as a decision. Vaping in public now looks like an untreated condition to a lot of people.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Reduced-pleasure reports hold at ~10–15% of long-term users. The Jun 2031 retatrutide data put a number on it: ~9% vs ~4% at top dose, dose-dependent. Marketers took the label line as proof of efficacy. About 2.7M adults use 'focus/calm' subscriptions at $199–279/month, counted inside the cash and gray shares, and roughly a third are employer-reimbursed.
interior_life.framing: A feature with a footnote. Brands sell 'quiet'. The DoD calls it 'craving resilience' in AUD and tobacco materials. Clinicians say 'reward modulation'. Users still say 'the grey' and lower the dose.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Police departments use DOJ COPS wellness grants to fund AUD and cessation semaglutide for officers, and unions argue over whether it can appear in a fitness-for-duty file. Hospitals offer 'shift stability' low-dose programmes to night nurses. Under the FAA's 2031 policy, pilots may fly after two months at a stable dose. Sales and creative staff still go off-dose before pitches.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Off-dose art is now a genre with its own festival slot at SXSW. Sports betting handle is softer in high-uptake states. Bars in military towns host 'one-drink nights'.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists ask about dose and now about bimagrumab-related body changes. Couples schedule dose holidays. Some military spouses say that coming home on the drug changed the marriage's tempo more than the deployment did.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Medicare Act passed with bipartisan votes. The fights are over fracture warnings, the Indian import alert and whether the Pentagon is 'medicating readiness'. Talk radio's 'pacification pills' line now targets the military programme. Candidates are no longer asked whether they are 'on'. They are asked why if they are off.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on indications and payment (vaping cessation, oral AUD, MariTide, the bimagrumab combination). Safety enforcement now centres on muscle and bone: class Warnings upgrade, statutory DEXA, required post-approval fracture-outcome trial. The import alert on Indian API serves both supply safety and gray-market control, and it hit the HRSA supply chain too.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Medicare Obesity and Metabolic Health Act makes Part D coverage permanent ($50 copay, $285 blended payment) and gives 90% FMAP for Medicaid incretins with body-composition visits. HRSA was renewed at $5.8B and remains discretionary. The ACA cessation mandate and AUD parity continue. No one is mandated to take the drug, but in the military the drug counts toward meeting a mandated standard.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged: ≥80% PDC, quarterly weigh-ins, 12-month lockout. Two more states joined. The Medicaid FMAP standard adds DEXA or bioimpedance visits, which makes body composition a recorded eligibility variable. HRSA sites still require only refill pickup.
state.workforce_or_military: The FY2032 NDAA and DoD Metabolic Readiness Instruction (Feb 2032) cover incretins for active and reserve personnel through TRICARE to meet body-composition standards and treat AUD and tobacco use. Initiation is barred during the first 8 weeks of basic training after the stress-fracture cluster. The FAA permits pilots on stable doses. DOJ COPS grants fund police programmes. DOT apnea screening still steers drivers to tirzepatide.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Apr 2031 import alert and the second Section 232 tariff step strained relations with India, which filed a WTO consultation request. Generic liraglutide makers are building US fill-finish capacity with DoD Defense Production Act Title III money. The incretin supply chain now sits on the defense-critical list.

events.event: FDA approves semaglutide as an adjunct for e-cigarette and vaping cessation in adults and extends the alcohol use disorder indication to oral semaglutide; USPSTF issues a draft grade B recommendation, bringing both under the ACA preventive mandate's two-course coverage

FDA import alert on three Indian semaglutide API makers coincides with a sterility recall by the largest HRSA generic liraglutide supplier and the second Section 232 tariff step; TrumpRx cash prices rise to $399 and $499, and the HRSA liraglutide contract price rises from $85 to $120

JAMA Medicare claims study finds a 1.36 hip-fracture hazard ratio in long-term users over 65; FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication moving lean-mass and bone loss into class Warnings and recommending DEXA monitoring

Congress passes the Medicare Obesity and Metabolic Health Act in the year-end health package, making Part D incretin coverage permanent from January 2032 at a $50 copay with statutory DEXA checks, and giving 90% federal match to Medicaid programmes that adopt body-composition visits

Pentagon issues its Metabolic Readiness Instruction under the FY2032 NDAA, covering incretins for service members to meet body-composition standards and treat alcohol and tobacco use, while barring new starts in basic training after a stress-fracture cluster

FDA approves Lilly's bimagrumab for use with tirzepatide on lean-mass and strength endpoints, with a required fracture-outcome trial; the $2,149 regimen launches on allocation as Lilly advertises an end to 'skinny-frail'

open_tensions: The muscle-preserving combination is sold as the answer to the fracture wave, but it has no fracture data, costs $2,149 a month, and has no Medicare formulary decision. The older women at highest risk are the least likely to get it, while fintech men in Charlotte already have it.

Public payers now cover 38% of users, and the government also enforces against the Indian supply that feeds HRSA generics and the gray market. The next appropriations fight and the 2033 generic entry will decide whether public expansion can be paid for.

The military now treats the drug as part of readiness while TRADOC investigates stress fractures in recruits. A body-composition standard that is met pharmacologically raises the question of whether stopping becomes a fitness-for-duty issue.

Reward blunting has an FDA-recognised number and a marketing department. Employer-paid 'focus' subscriptions and police wellness programmes are testing whether a dose record can enter an employment file.
still_true: Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation for two 90-day courses a year.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: One in Four, Paid by Washington: The Drug Became Infrastructure. Now It's Coming for Your Hips
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about sixty-three million American adults are on an incretin drug, nearly one in four. Washington now pays for more of them than employers do. In December 2031 the GLP-1 Bridge, a demonstration that had been renewed twice, became permanent Part D coverage in a year-end health package. The copay stayed at fifty dollars, and Medicare pays a blended $285 a month. Medicaid programmes that adopt a body-composition visit get ninety cents on the dollar from Washington, and thirty-four states have signed up. The free-clinic programme for generic liraglutide survived another appropriations cycle. Taken together, public payers now cover thirty-eight percent of users, against thirty-four percent for commercial plans.

It grew while prices rose again. In April 2031 the FDA put three Indian semaglutide ingredient makers on import alert. That same month the biggest supplier of the free clinics' generic liraglutide recalled its lots for sterility, and the tariff took its second scheduled step. The cash portal went to $399 for semaglutide and $499 for tirzepatide. The import alert shrank the gray market from about one user in six to one in seven. It also raised the cost of the government's own free programme, and India took the matter to the WTO.

The new indications kept bringing in people who had never thought of themselves as patients. Vaping cessation was approved in February 2031, and alcohol treatment became available as a pill. Young adults who vape and men who drink too much now fill a prescription under rules written for smoking and mental-health parity.

Then the hips. In September 2031 a study of Medicare claims found that older Americans on the drug for more than two years broke their hips about a third more often than those who were not. That works out to roughly fifteen thousand extra hip fractures a year, concentrated in women over seventy. The FDA moved muscle and bone loss into the class Warnings section. The new Medicare law turned DEXA scans and strength counselling into statute. YMCAs fill with seventy-year-olds learning deadlifts, and grocery aisles fill with calcium-fortified protein. A year later the FDA approved Lilly's bimagrumab for use with tirzepatide. The approval rested on preserved muscle and strength. Fracture outcomes have not been studied yet. Lilly's advertising says 'skinny-frail' is over. The regimen lists at $2,149, is allocated, and is not yet on any Medicare formulary. The people who have it are mostly the people who already had coaches.

The state has started treating the drug as readiness. The Pentagon covers it for service members who need to meet body-composition standards and for drinking and tobacco use. The FAA lets pilots fly on a stable dose. Police departments pay for it with Justice Department wellness grants, and hospitals offer night nurses a low-dose 'shift stability' programme. When trainees at Fort Jackson and Lackland started showing up with stress fractures, the Army barred new starts during basic training. Soldiers who were already on the drug stayed on it.

In San Antonio, a city of bases and retirees, the drug is unremarkable. Being off it is what people ask about. The retatrutide study finally put a number on the quieting effect, about one in eleven at the top dose, and the wellness brands that sell it as 'focus' put that number in their ads until the FTC stopped them. Musicians still tour off-dose. Spirits volumes are falling for a fifth straight year, and two states' tobacco-settlement bonds have been downgraded. From outside, the country looks steady, sober and lean. Inside, a grandmother's hip, a recruit's shin and a dose record in a police file are all being argued over, and none of the arguments is settled.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rosa Villarreal is sixty-eight. She takes her shot on Sunday mornings before Mass, in the thigh, the way the pharmacist at the H-E-B on Bandera showed her. Fifty dollars this month, same as last month. The card says Part D now, not Bridge. She doesn't know what changed.

Monday is the DEXA. The technician, a girl from Harlandale, tells her to lie still and not to worry. Later the doctor shows her two colours on a screen and says 'osteopenia, left hip' as kindly as she can. She writes Rosa a slip for a strength class and asks how much protein she eats. Rosa lies a little.

The class is at the Y. Eleven women and one man named Hector lift kettlebells that look like toys. The instructor counts in English and then in Spanish. Rosa's arms shake. She likes it more than she expected to.

At home her husband, Ernesto, eats a whole plate of fideo. He stopped the drug in 2030 and says it made him feel like a television left on with no sound. Their daughter calls this 'Dad's choice' in a tone Rosa doesn't like.

Her grandson Marcos calls from Lackland. He's in week six and they won't start him on the pen until he graduates. Half his flight is waiting too. He says his shins hurt. She tells him to drink milk.

On the news a man in a good suit says 'skinny-frail is over'. Rosa asks the pharmacist the next day whether Medicare pays for that one. The pharmacist laughs, not unkindly, and shakes her head.
